newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania, Hungary to sign free trade pact by May.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania, Hungary to sign free trade pact by May.

text.p: Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius on Wednesday said the Baltic state plans to sign a free trade deal with Hungary by May.
The deal would remove the last obstacle for Lithuania's entry into the Central European Free Trade Association (CEFTA).
Vagnorius' office said the premier met earlier with Hungarian President Arpad Goncz, on a state visit to Lithuania.

"Much attention was paid to economic, cultural and scientific cooperation, Lithuanian membership in CETFA and integration into the European Union (EU) and NATO," Vagnorius' office said in a statement.
"Before May 1997 it is planned to draw up and sign a free trade agreement," the statement added.
Lithuania has signed free-trade pacts with other CEFTA members Poland, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Slovenia.
Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas said yesterday that his country aimed to be in CEFTA this year.
As well as orienting itself to central and eastern Europe, Lithuania also aims to boost ties with the West and has applied to become a full member of the European Union (EU).
Lithuania exported $10 million worth of goods to Hungary last year and imported $39 million from Hungary.
